candidate.title: Drop-ChIP/scChIP-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina droplet-based single-cell ChIP schematic, clarified by the Rotem et al. 2015 Drop-ChIP implementation. The card uses Drop-ChIP and scChIP-Seq as aliases for this workflow; scChIP-Seq here does not mean every single-cell ChIP-seq implementation. The opening nucleosome cartoon introduces chromatin as the target. There is one merging barcode input and one downstream route, with no depicted alternative assay. The antibody epitope is unspecified in the image; the inspected paper demonstrates H3K4me3 and H3K4me2. Paper-supported droplet release and broad library-conversion interfaces bridge the drawn stages without importing the complete protocol. Fusion supplies the labeling substrates and reagents; the paper places the ligation incubation after physical droplet collection and before compartment release. The graph represents those boundaries separately.

method_scopes.rationale: Applies to the droplet implementation named by this card. Its description explicitly aliases Drop-ChIP and scChIP-seq, and the cited primary paper describes this same droplet capture, MNase fragmentation, barcode ligation, pooled ChIP and sequencing route. The shared scope follows this explicit identity and content match, not similarity to other assays. Within this implementation, fusion supplies the labeling reagents, fused droplets are collected, and ligation proceeds in the collected emulsion before release for ChIP. The additional local ligation interface resolves that staging without adding an alternative workflow.
